about: workflow:keep-practice-cards-and-grades: a person's cards to get right every time (a word, a habit, a fact), each grade they give a card, and their spacing policy, kept in the person's own store. It replaces the record half of tools/practice-and-review (read-data/practice-cards.mjs, tool:practice, whose whole job except the timing was keeping cards, grades and the policy through the retired records door). When a card is due is worked out by the values-in engine in the same folder (tool:schedule-next-review and tool:list-what-is-due), which takes the grades the store returns and the policy as values (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep practice cards and their grades
payload.job: Keep the person's cards (a prompt, its answer, a deck, an optional why and source), each grade they give a card as its own entry, and their spacing policy, in the person's own store: a card added again keeps its progress and refreshes its answer and why; a grade is only ever added; a removed card leaves its grades behind; and a read gives the cards with their standing folded from their grades, the cards due now, and how many are due.
payload.produces: The store's own card, grade and policy objects, proven on the example attempts in PostgreSQL (PGlite) and a folder of JSON files: every attempt kept, refused or answered, and every answer the same as the old tool's. Each morning at 09:00 (America/Chicago until the person's AI sets their own zone when it switches the wake on), a remind that finds cards due tells the person once.

source.from: tools/practice-and-review/read-data/practice-cards.mjs (tool:practice) and read-data/practice-cards.json, at trillion-workshop origin/main bb8022539 before this change
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job. The card id is a stable key from the deck and the prompt: 'card:' + deck + ':' + the first 16 hex characters of the BLAKE3 hash of deck, a zero byte and prompt (the old tool's cardId, so existing cards keep their ids). A due time is never stored: it is folded from the grades each time by tool:list-what-is-due and tool:schedule-next-review, and the mastery number is computed from the state the engine returns: round(min(1, interval_days / policy.mastered_at_days) x 1000), or nothing when the policy has no mastered_at_days, and 0 while the state's reps is 0 (a lapse starts a card over, as the first tool's mastery did: its test asserted a missed card has mastery 0). A cards read also answers the mean mastery of the cards it shows, round(sum / count), 0 when it shows none. The policy is the person's: it comes with the request or is kept as the policy record with the id asked for (default: 'default'); there is no default policy. The words the old tool sent back are the person's to keep: no card is 'No card <card id> is kept.'; remind says '1 card is due to practise now.', '<count> cards are due to practise now.' or 'Nothing is due to practise now.'; a due list shows 20 cards unless the request asks for a limit; an add that would keep a new card past input.max_cards is refused with 'An account practises at most <max_cards> cards. Remove one first.'; a card added again may change its answer without touching its source_ref (kept), and a source_ref given as null clears it.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the cards are kept, when they already are

operations.description: Each operation: add (prompt, answer, deck, why, source_ref; a source_ref left out keeps the card's earlier one, null clears it), grade (card_id, grade, policy or policy_id), remove (card_id), cards (deck; answers each card's mastery and the mean), due (deck, limit), remind (tells the person when cards are due, once a day)

max_cards.description: Optional. The most cards the person keeps; an add that would keep a new card past it is refused (a card added again is not a new card). Left out, no limit.

notices_database.description: Optional. The name of the person's own database the notices live in. When given, a remind that finds cards due tells the person once a day through workflow:tell-the-person; left out, remind only answers the sentence.

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the cards are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them, and show them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: a card object keyed by its card id (prompt, answer, deck, why, source_ref, added_at), a grade object that is only ever added (card id, grade word, at), and a policy object keyed by its policy id (the numbers and grade words the policy names). Keep a primary key on the card id, a check that the grade names an existing card when it is written, and no delete of a grade when its card is removed. Submit the objects made.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, and with the policy {initial_ease 2.5, min_ease 1.3, first_interval_days 1, second_interval_days 6, lapse_below_quality 0.6, mastered_at_days 30, grade_quality {miss 0, shaky 0.6, solid 0.8, instant 1}} kept as policy 'default', max_cards 3 and the notices kept in the same throwaway place, run these attempts in order on the day each is given (day 0 is 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z; CARD_1 is card:sample-deck:4fd68f6ab03764f9 and CARD_2 is card:general:1212e13cd674cd15, CARD_3 is card:general:f2345125af637f79, the ids the old tool gives): [{"day": 0, "operation": "add", "prompt": "A sample word", "answer": "Its sample meaning", "deck": "sample-deck"}, {"day": 0, "operation": "add", "prompt": "A sample word", "answer": "Its sample meaning, again", "why": "a note", "deck": "sample-deck"}, {"day": 0, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Second card", "answer": "Second meaning"}, {"day": 0, "operation": "add", "answer": "no prompt"}, {"day": 0, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Bad deck", "answer": "x", "deck": "a b"}, {"day": 0, "operation": "grade", "card_id": "card:general:missing", "grade": "solid"}, {"day": 1, "operation": "grade", "card_id": "CARD_1", "grade": "solid"}, {"day": 2, "operation": "grade", "card_id": "CARD_1", "grade": "miss"}, {"day": 3, "operation": "due"}, {"day": 5, "operation": "due"}, {"day": 5, "operation": "remind"}, {"day": 5, "operation": "cards", "deck": "sample-deck"}, {"day": 6, "operation": "grade", "card_id": "CARD_2", "grade": "shaky"}, {"day": 7, "operation": "remove", "card_id": "CARD_2"}, {"day": 8, "operation": "cards"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Third card", "answer": "Third meaning", "source_ref": "fixture:third"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Fourth card", "answer": "Fourth meaning"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Fifth card", "answer": "Fifth meaning"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Third card", "answer": "Third meaning edited"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "grade", "card_id": "CARD_3", "grade": "solid"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "cards"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "add", "prompt": "Third card", "answer": "Third meaning edited", "source_ref": null}, {"day": 9, "operation": "remind"}, {"day": 9, "operation": "remind"}]. Rules: an add needs a prompt and an answer; a deck is letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores; a card added again with the same deck and prompt keeps its progress and takes the new answer and why; a grade needs an existing card; a remove keeps the card's grades; an add past max_cards for a new card is refused, and one for a card already kept is not; a card added again without a source_ref keeps its source_ref, and one given null clears it; a missed card has mastery 0; a cards read answers the mean mastery of the cards it shows; a remind that finds cards due keeps one notice in the notices through workflow:tell-the-person under the key 'practice:<that day>' (title 'Practise now', kind 'practice'), however often it runs that day. The fold of the grades into each card's standing is the values-in engine's (tool:list-what-is-due with the cards as prompts, the grades as responses and the policy; tool:schedule-next-review for one grade, with the card's prior state). Submit outcomes (one per attempt, kept, refused or answered) and the answer: the read-back of each attempt's answer, with the remind sentence, the mastery, the mean mastery and the notice count shown.

checks.says: Each attempt is kept, refused or answered as the intent says
The store's own objects give every expected answer

steps.title: Keep this run's operations
steps.do: Run each operation in the request in order, through the store's own objects and the values-in tools: an add writes or refreshes the card and keeps its progress and, when the request gives no source_ref, the card's earlier source_ref (null clears it), and a new card past input.max_cards is refused; a grade computes the card's next state with tool:schedule-next-review from the card's last state (folded from its grades) and the policy, then adds one grade entry; a remove deletes the card and keeps its grades; a card, due or remind read folds every card's standing with tool:list-what-is-due and answers the cards (each with its mastery and lapse_count), the count and the sentence, and a cards read also answers the mean mastery of the cards it shows; a remind that finds cards due, when input.notices_database is given, runs workflow:tell-the-person with that database, the title 'Practise now', the sentence as the body, kind 'practice' and the key 'practice:<today's date>', so the person is told once a day however often it runs. Submit results (one per operation: the answer it gave, or the refusal's words), kept_records (the card ids and grade entries kept), and found_records (each card read back). With no operations, submit empty lists.

checks.says: Every card read back was kept

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes every card with its grades, or one card with its grades; the policy is deleted only with the person's word. Nothing keeps a copy outside the store.
